v.q: What is the minimum Java version required by Spring Boot 3?
v.w: Spring Boot 3 is built on Spring Framework 6, which requires Java 17 or later. Java 21 is supported and adds virtual threads.

v.q: Which Java version is too old for Spring Boot 3?
v.w: Spring Boot 3 requires Java 17 or later.

v.q: What is the biggest source-level change when migrating from Spring Boot 2 to 3?
o: Gradle replaces Maven as the build tool
v.w: Jakarta EE 9+ renamed the packages, so imports such as `javax.persistence` become `jakarta.persistence`. OpenRewrite recipes automate most of it.

v.q: Which import must change when migrating to Spring Boot 3?
v.w: Jakarta EE 9 renamed the javax packages, so all Jakarta imports change.

v.q: How do you turn on virtual threads for a Spring Boot 3.2+ web app on Java 21?
v.w: Blocking code keeps its simple style while the server handles requests on cheap virtual threads. Watch for pinning in `synchronized` blocks.

v.q: Which Java version is needed for virtual threads in Spring Boot 3.2?
v.w: Virtual threads were finalised in Java 21. Boot enables them with a single property.

v.q: What is Spring AOT used for?
o: Generating code and hints at build time for faster, native-ready startup
Making the unit tests run faster inside the CI pipeline
Compiling Java source code into JavaScript for browsers
Hot reloading changed classes inside a production server
v.w: Ahead-of-time processing resolves bean definitions at build time. GraalVM native images need that because of the closed-world assumption.

o: It prepares code and hints at build time
It reloads classes at run time
v.w: AOT processing generates what native images and faster startup need.

v.q: What does a GraalVM native image trade for its fast startup and low memory?
o: Longer builds, plus limits on reflection and dynamic features
Loss of support for ordinary Java classes and interfaces
Losing the ability to run on Linux container hosts
Giving up the use of Spring beans in the application
v.w: Reflection, proxies and resources must be known at build time (hints). Peak throughput may also be lower than a warmed-up JIT JVM.

v.q: Which is NOT a limit of a GraalVM native image?
v.w: Native images run well on Linux and in containers. The costs are build time and a closed-world model.

v.q: Which class replaces `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` in modern Spring Security?
v.w: You now declare one or more `SecurityFilterChain` beans using the lambda DSL of `HttpSecurity`.

v.q: Which style configures Spring Security 6 without the old adapter?
v.w: The adapter was removed. Declare beans instead.

v.q: What is the standard way to return errors in Spring 6 / Boot 3 REST APIs?
o: A plain string holding the stack trace
An HTML error page returned to every client
Always `200 OK` with an error field
v.w: Enable with `spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true` or return `ProblemDetail` from an `@ExceptionHandler`.

v.q: Which type returns RFC 9457 errors in Spring 6?
v.w: ProblemDetail carries type, title, status and detail in a standard format.

v.q: What does the Observation API in Spring 6 allow?
o: Instrumenting code once to get metrics, traces and log context
Watching files on disk and reloading them when they change
Observing user behaviour in the browser for analytics
Replacing the logging framework that the application uses
v.w: It builds on Micrometer so one instrumentation point feeds Prometheus metrics and distributed tracing together.

v.q: Which statement about the Observation API is NOT true?
v.w: One observation can feed metrics, traces and log context through handlers.
